screening_results.reason: This is an empirical, English-language MRI VBM study comparing alcohol-dependent patients and controls and reports voxel-wise asymmetry (AI) analyses and a global Dice coefficient (meets I2). Voxelwise asymmetry results are reported (I4) and participant details and methods are provided (I5). However, the paper does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast comparing gray matter volume (standard voxelwise GM volume contrasts) of substance users vs controls; it reports group differences in asymmetry indices rather than direct GM volume differences, so it does not meet I3. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or nonempirical paper) are triggered.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing grey-matter volumes between cocaine-use disorder (stimulant) participants and healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (CUD vs HC and CUD vs GD) with cluster-based FWE-corrected results and coordinate/figure/table reporting, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant demographics (age, sex) and MRI details (3T Siemens Trio, MPRAGE acquisition) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL VBM, randomise) are provided. The study directly addresses the meta-analysis objective of structural GM differences in substance users (stimulants) vs controls. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical human data). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore include.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI VBM study comparing current-smokers (nicotine users) with never-smokers and reports whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts. The paper provides voxelwise whole-brain results (FWE-corrected across the whole brain) with peak coordinates (Table 2) and figures, and includes participant age/sex, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment of methodology and outcomes. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective (nicotine class).

This is an empirical human sMRI (VBM) study comparing heavy cannabis users to matched non-using controls, addressing structural GM differences relevant to the review. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected results with significant clusters in hippocampus/amygdala and superior temporal gyrus), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group or voxelwise results. Key methodological details are provided (3T MRI field strength; preprocessing/statistical software: SPM/VBM8 and DARTEL; participant demographics and age/sex information are reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of GM differences in cannabis users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing gray matter volume between cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The paper explicitly reports whole-brain VBM analyses (noting whole-brain between-group differences were nonsignificant) and then reports ROI follow-ups; the main text clearly indicates voxelwise whole-brain results were performed and available. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8), and participant demographics are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not meet exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; empirical human data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol users (MRS, VBM, SBM) but it does not include a control group or report any whole‑brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls. The analyses are correlational/ROI-based within a single sample of drinkers (right mid-insula ROI), so it fails key inclusion criteria (I2 and I3). It therefore meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). The paper does report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (satisfied I5).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of cocaine users that reports whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of gray matter volume between substance users (iCUD) and healthy controls. The manuscript includes whole-brain SPM8/VBM8 analyses with reported significant group effects and coordinates, describes participants’ age/sex, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software, and provides full introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical GMV MRI studies with whole-brain between-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter volume (and thickness) between amphetamine/MDMA users (experienced and low-exposure) and drug-naïve controls. The study performed fully automated whole-brain vertex-wise analyses (Freesurfer QDEC for cortical thickness/volume; FSL/FIRST for subcortical shape) with correction for multiple comparisons and reports group contrasts (experienced vs controls, etc.). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons of stimulant users vs controls. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, English-language MRI study with whole-brain voxelwise VBM and TBSS analyses (clusters reported) and adequate methodological details (age/sex, 3T field strength, preprocessing/software), it does not present any whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users versus controls. Instead, the paper reports continuous GLM associations between AUDIT score or days of cannabis use and GM/WM measures across pooled samples. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I2 (studies assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of methamphetamine users and controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software details (meets I5). However, the manuscript does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls comparing gray-matter volume (I3 not met). The reported whole-brain voxelwise results focus on group-by-midbrain/striatal D2/D3 BP interactions and correlations with craving, not a direct users-vs-controls GM volume contrast; the authors state they do not focus on previously reported group differences. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only paper or non-empirical article) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study that compares gray matter structure between substance-dependent individuals and nondependent controls using whole-brain FreeSurfer parcellation (82 ROIs covering cortical and subcortical regions). It reports participant demographics (age, sex), scanner/acquisition details (in supplement), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer; linear mixed-effects models and SVM). The analysis includes whole-brain between-group contrasts (model 1 and model 2) across all ROIs rather than limited small ROIs, satisfying the review’s whole-brain requirement. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM study) and I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts), as well as I4 (reporting of results in main text/tables/figures) and I5 (reports age/sex and preprocessing/statistics; scanner details in supplement). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing grey matter volumes between adolescent/young adult heavy alcohol users and matched controls (meets I2). It reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8) (meets I5). Voxelwise/coordinate results are presented (figures/tables) for ROI analyses (meets I4). However, the authors state that the whole-brain VBM analysis showed no group differences and that subsequent findings derive from ROI analyses with small-volume correction; the whole-brain contrast produced no qualifying significant results. Therefore the study effectively reports only ROI-positive findings with no qualifying whole-brain results, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criterion I3 (report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast with qualifying results) is not met. Consequently the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM MRI study comparing 30 alcohol-dependent patients with matched controls, reporting whole-brain between-group GM volume comparisons and voxelwise regression analyses linking GM volume to Iowa Gambling Task performance. Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing (VBM5/SPM5), and participant demographics (age/sex distribution). Voxelwise results are reported in the results with anatomical localization/coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets the review objective (structural GM differences in a substance-using group — alcohol) and satisfies inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent (treatment-naive) subjects and controls. The paper reports whole-brain measures (total cortical gray matter) and regional cortical volumes derived from a whole-brain segmentation mapped to Talairach ROIs (15 cortical ROIs), providing between-group contrasts (HD vs LD) and regional localization (prefrontal and parietal reductions). Participant age and sex (male-only), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical approaches are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It is not limited to single small ROI analyses and thus does not meet exclusion E5. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2 and I3, and reports participant/MRI details per I5.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed MRI VBM study (cocaine-dependent patients vs matched controls) that reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts and provides MNI coordinates and statistics for significant GM volume differences (striatal and supramarginal gyrus). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM toolbox, SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, not merely an abstract. The study is not ROI-only and is original human MRI research, meeting the review’s objective to identify GM structural alterations in stimulant users. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent subjects and controls (meets I2) and reports participant/MRI details (meets I5). However, the analyses are based on automated region-of-interest (subcortical and hippocampal subfield) segmentation rather than any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain GM contrast (I3), which is not present. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed human sMRI study (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between substance-using groups (cannabis-dependent, nicotine-dependent, co-users) and healthy controls. The study used whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (VBM with DARTEL, SPM8) and reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and regional findings presented in text/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant ages/sex, scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This study is excluded because it is an experimental, non-human (vervet monkey) methamphetamine administration study rather than an empirical MRI study of human substance users versus human controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (provides voxel-wise/whole-brain between-group contrasts within specified search volumes), I4 (voxelwise results are reported/illustrated), I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study does not assess grey matter differences in human substance users vs human controls; subjects are non-human animals). Exclusion criteria met: none (E5 and E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol dependence using deformation-based morphometry to assess grey matter and white matter differences between recovering alcoholics and light-drinking controls. The full text contains introduction, methods (including MRI acquisition at 1.5T and voxelwise registration/analysis), results, and discussion. Whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts are reported (ANCOVA of deformation maps at 1 week abstinence; longitudinal voxelwise maps comparing groups), and cluster-level significant regions are described. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical methods are provided. The paper is not an ROI-only study or a non-empirical paper. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons and should be included.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that reports whole-brain between-group GM contrasts comparing alcohol users (alcohol use disorder/abusers) and matched controls. The paper provides voxelwise results and coordinates, uses SPM5/VBM processing, and reports participant demographics (male, n=24 per group, age range), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Findings include regional GM volume reductions in prefrontal regions and correlational voxelwise analyses with impulsivity. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Limitations) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI VBM study comparing smokers (nicotine users) to never-smokers reporting voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts. The paper reports modulated (volume) and unmodulated (density) whole-brain VBM results (FDR-corrected at P<0.05), provides tables/figures of regional findings, and describes participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between regular cannabis users and occasional user controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts with cluster coordinates and voxelwise correlation results (monthly frequency vs GM) and describes methods (3T MRI field strength, SPM8/DARTEL preprocessing, statistical thresholds). Participant demographics (male, ages 18–30) and exclusion of other drugs are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volumes between cocaine-dependent individuals and non-drug-using controls (stimulant class relevant). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts were conducted and significant peaks are reported (MNI space) with family-wise error correction (pFWE < 0.05). Participant demographics (age, all-male sample), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between nicotine-dependent smokers and nonsmoker controls (I2 satisfied). The paper reports voxelwise between-group GM contrasts (significant clusters in bilateral Crus I) and indicates that whole-brain DARTEL analyses were also performed (results referenced in Supplementary Materials), which satisfies the requirement for a whole-brain between-group contrast (I3 satisfied; I4 satisfied because voxelwise results are reported in figures/tables and supplementary materials). Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, SUIT, DPARSFA) are reported (I5 satisfied). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., this is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), though some whole-brain results are in supplement; confidence tempered slightly for that reason.

This is an empirical English MRI study (prenatal alcohol-exposed neonates vs unexposed controls) reporting gray matter volume differences and participant/MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses are atlas-based regional volumetric comparisons extracted from 90 AAL regions (ROI/parcellation-based), not voxelwise whole-brain statistical contrasts or VBM maps. The paper does not provide a qualifying voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrast; thus it falls under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast) and I4 (qualifying voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients and controls and reports gray and white matter volumes (I2 met). However, it does not report voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts or provide coordinate-based regional GM differences: analyses are global volumetric measures (ICV, total cerebral, gray/white matter volumes and ratios) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts) is not met. Because no qualifying whole-brain results are reported, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group GMV contrasts comparing cocaine USERS and CONTROLS. The paper describes full methods (participants, scanner field strength 3T, VBM preprocessing and statistical procedures including TFCE and permutation testing), reports results of whole-brain group comparisons and correlations with abstinence duration, and provides demographic information (male participants, mean age). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only (whole-brain VBM reported) and is empirical with original human MRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although sample size is modest and participants are male veterans, these are methodological limitations but do not disqualify the study from inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on GMV differences in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing grey matter between daily cannabis users and matched nonusers (adults and adolescents). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and FreeSurfer surface-based whole-brain analyses (in addition to ROI and shape analyses), meeting the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls; results (including null findings) are presented in the main text with methods and statistics. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL VBM, FreeSurfer, FIRST) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and is not a non-empirical paper. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet exclusion criteria E5 or E6.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM8/DARTEL) on T1-weighted scans (1.0T) comparing gray matter volume between alcohol users (various drinking levels) and matched abstainers. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise two-sample t-tests (and ROI SVC for parahippocampus) for drinkers versus controls and presents the results (null findings). It therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM study), I3 (reports whole-brain between-group contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results reported/available), and I5 (reports age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to assess gray matter density differences between cocaine (stimulant) users (current and abstainers) and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (tables and figures) comparing substance users vs controls, describes participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5 on MATLAB), and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter volumes between methamphetamine (stimulant) users and healthy controls. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study used whole-brain automated segmentation covering six main lobes and 17 subregions (i.e., whole-brain coverage) and reports between-group contrasts and drug-by-age interactions across these regions. Participant age/sex information, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL v3.3, SAS) are reported. Therefore it meets criteria for empirical MRI GM comparisons (I2), provides whole-brain between-group analyses (I3), allows that voxelwise/region results are available in text/tables/figures (I4), and reports key participant and acquisition/preprocessing details (I5). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter between opiate-dependent subjects (n=63) and matched healthy controls (n=46). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM99) with conservative corrected thresholds and lists regional findings (prefrontal, insular, temporal cortices) in tables/figures. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5T GE), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening (core sections present).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study that reports whole-brain vertex-wise and ROI-wise comparisons between heroin-dependent individuals and controls and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer). However, the study measures cortical thickness (surface-based morphometry) rather than grey matter (GM) volume. The meta-analysis inclusion criteria require studies assessing GM volume differences (I2) and whole-brain GM volume contrasts (I3). Therefore it does not meet I2 and I3, so it must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable. The abstract indicates an empirical English-language MRI VBM study comparing grey matter volume between synthetic cannabinoid users and healthy controls, so I2 is satisfied. However, I cannot verify that the paper reports a qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast (I3) or that voxelwise results/coordinates are provided in tables/figures/supplementary materials (I4). Key methodological details (participant ages, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are not fully available in the provided content (I5 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria are clearly met (E5, E6 not applicable). Because the full text (methods/results) is inaccessible, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria and must exclude this study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical, longitudinal MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between adolescents who initiated alcohol use (moderate and heavy) and no/low-drinking controls. The paper reports whole-brain cortical analyses using FreeSurfer parcellations (34 cortical ROIs) and surface maps with FDR-corrected regional differences, providing whole-brain between-group contrasts. Participant age/sex information and preprocessing/statistical software are reported; MRI acquisition details are described (supplement). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study directly comparing cigarette smokers to nonsmoking controls using voxel‑based morphometry and multivariate classification. The paper analyzes whole‑brain data (VBM preprocessing across the entire brain and a 1,024‑region whole‑brain parcellation), identifies discriminative ROIs that differentiate smokers and controls, and reports coordinates and region locations (Table 2 and figures), satisfying the requirement for whole‑brain results (coordinate/figure/tabulated results acceptable). Participant demographics (age/sex) and MRI details (3T scanner, MPRAGE sequence) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/VBM8, LIBSVM) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study comparing cocaine users (active and remitted) and controls and reports GMV differences using ROI analyses and exploratory whole-brain correlations. However, it does not report any whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts of substance users versus controls (the authors explicitly state they did not report whole-brain group differences). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI GMV study) and I5 (reports demographic/MRI/preprocessing details). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GMV contrast). Full text appears complete.

This study is a pathological postmortem volumetric study (ImageJ counting of coronal slices) rather than an in vivo MRI study, and it reports region-of-interest (ROI) analyses of selected gray-matter regions without any whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain between-group MRI contrasts. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: none. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls using MRI), I3 (does not report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of heavy nicotine users (smokers) versus matched nonsmoking controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group GM contrasts (with MNI coordinates and significance values) and also provides multivariate SVM discrimination maps. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM) are reported. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons between substance users (nicotine) and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cannabis users (occasional and frequent) to non-users using whole-brain analyses of gray matter metrics (volumes, cortical thickness, gray matter density). Methods report acquisition (3T), preprocessing software (ANTs, FreeSurfer), and participant age/sex. Results present whole-brain/global/lobar/regional comparisons (with supplementary tables/figures) and coordinate-style/region-level reporting. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume analyses and provides sufficient methodological detail for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey-matter volume between methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) users and control groups. The full text includes introduction, methods (1.5T MRI, VBM8/SPM8 preprocessing), results, and discussion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (cross-sectional ANCOVA and longitudinal flexible factorial analyses) with cluster-wise and FWE-corrected results, and details participant age/sex and other acquisition/analysis parameters. These features satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM volume comparisons with whole-brain results; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete for screening (supplementary data noted but not required).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing grey matter volumes in alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients and controls (meets I2). The paper reports detailed participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, SUIT, Ceres, Hopkins pipelines) (meets I5). However, the analyses are atlas-based lobular/parcellation and region-wise volumetry of the cerebellum (ROI/atlas analyses) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast. No whole-brain voxelwise or coordinate-based between-group results are provided, so it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI/atlas analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between heavy-drinking adolescents and light-drinking controls (meets I2). Participant characteristics and methodological details (ages, sex, MRI acquisition and preprocessing) are reported (meets I5). However, the analyses were limited to 24 a priori regions-of-interest (mean ROI GM values were used) rather than reporting any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or providing whole-brain coordinate tables/voxelwise results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and does not provide qualifying voxelwise results (I4). Per exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results), this study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between heroin-dependent subjects and matched healthy controls. The methods describe whole-brain, voxel-by-voxel ANOVA analyses (SPM2) with reported between-group differences (p<0.001 uncorrected) across multiple brain regions, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, VBM) are reported. The study addresses the opioids class relevant to the review objective and reports group contrasts of substance users vs controls. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing gray matter between nicotine-dependent smokers and nonsmoking controls using both ROI and whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts with voxelwise results and peak coordinates (including corrected p-values and x,y,z locations), uses SPM99 for preprocessing/analysis, specifies MRI field strength (1.5 T), and reports participant age and sex. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; is empirical). Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing alcohol-dependent (AD) subjects (N=119) with matched healthy controls (N=97). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise univariate analyses (group contrast control>AD, age regressions, lifetime consumption regressions) and uses atlas-based regional contrasts and a whole-brain brain-age model. Methods include MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, VBM8), and participant age/sex details. Results present whole-brain maps and cross-regional contrast estimates (figures and supplementary tables/contrast estimates referenced). Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter (GM) volume between heroin-dependent subjects and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (optimized VBM) and lists significant clusters (right PFC BA9, left SMC BA6, bilateral CC BA24) with cluster-level statistics and references to Table 1/Figure 1, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2/SPM2 and smoothing/modulation parameters) are detailed. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) apply. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review (opioid/heroin class) and should be included.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that reports whole-brain between-group (cocaine-dependent vs. cocaine-naive controls) comparisons of gray matter concentration. The methods specify MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99), and participant demographics (ages, all-male sample). Results present whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with corrected cluster-level findings in orbitofrontal, insular, cingulate, and temporal cortices. The study addresses the meta-analysis objective (stimulant class — cocaine). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorders (substance users) compared to matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with voxel-wise between-group contrasts and significant clusters (left frontal/temporal/parietal and lateral frontal clusters), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Voxelwise results are reported and corroborated with ROI analysis; MRI field strength (3T), participant age/sex, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FIRST, FSL-VBM, FAST) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of GM volume differences in substance (alcohol) users vs. controls.

This is an empirical MRI study comparing cortical gray matter volumes between chronic alcoholic men and healthy controls with longitudinal between-group contrasts. The paper reports segmented cortical GM volumes summed over slices and compares rates of change between alcoholics (abstainers and relapsers) and controls, representing whole-brain GM volume comparisons rather than ROI-only analyses. Participant sex is reported (58 alcoholic men); full methods and results are available in the full text. The study is thus relevant to alcohol (one of the review drug classes) and meets the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical whole-brain GM volume comparison studies.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescent smokers (users) to nonsmoking controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and reporting significant GM volume differences (vmPFC) with voxel coordinates and cluster-size correction. Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T across sites), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 for VBM), and whole-brain results and coordinates. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (whole-brain GM volume contrasts between substance users and controls for nicotine). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of cocaine (a stimulant) users vs controls and reports gray-matter-related measures (cortical thickness/surface area and subcortical volumes), satisfying inclusion criteria I2 and I5. However, the study restricted analyses to pre-defined frontal ROIs rather than reporting any whole-brain/voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast reported). Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (whole-brain GM contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an original, English-language structural MRI study (3T scanner) that assesses gray-matter-related measures (global cortical gray matter volume and vertexwise whole-brain cortical thickness) comparing prenatal cannabis/tobacco-exposed children to controls. The paper reports whole-brain vertexwise between-group contrasts with clusterwise correction (FreeSurfer QDEC) and provides cluster results in the main text (satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting). Participant age, sex distribution, field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the primary vertexwise outcome is cortical thickness rather than VBM GM density, it is a valid whole-brain grey-matter structural measure relevant to the review objective. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder to controls and reports participant ages, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/segmentation tools (FAST, AFNI) (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper reports manually-traced hippocampal (ROI) volumes and global tissue ratios and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts or coordinate tables/figures for voxelwise results. Therefore it does not satisfy the required whole-brain between-group GM analysis (I3) and does not provide qualifying voxelwise results (I4). Because the study reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only studies) applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of former heroin (opioid) users vs controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-tests with multiple-comparison correction; peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes are reported. Participant demographics (age range, group counts), MRI field strength (3T), acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are provided. The study directly addresses opioid-related GM alterations, matching the review objective. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Hence it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing cigarette smokers (nicotine users) and never-smokers using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (VBM) with cluster coordinates (MNI x = -34, y = 22, z = 14) and details of preprocessing/statistical software and MRI field strength (3T, SPM8, VBM8, FreeSurfer, ANTS). Participant demographics (age range, matching, and sex balance) are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for grey matter volume differences in nicotine users vs. controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing gray matter volume between college-aged binge-drinking (alcohol) subjects and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (group × gender factorial model) with cluster- and voxel-level FWE-corrected results and specific MNI coordinates (ventral striatum SVC reported). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Tim Trio), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The article is an empirical, English-language MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent users and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (CUD vs CON) with results presented in tables/figures (coordinates and SPM5 results), and performs voxelwise regression analyses with lifetime drug use. Participant demographics (age, sex—male-only sample), MRI field strength (4 Tesla), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of structural GM differences in stimulant users.

The study reports an empirical VBM MRI comparison of heroin-dependent men vs controls (I2) and provides voxel coordinates/figures (I4) and participant and MRI preprocessing details (I5). However, the only significant GMV finding was obtained using a small-volume/ROI familywise error correction restricted to the DLPFC; no whole-brain positive GMV coordinates/contrasts are reported (whole-brain tests were null aside from ROI-SVC). This means the paper effectively reports ROI-constrained results only and therefore meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I3 (reporting at least one whole-brain between-group GMV contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete. Exclude for E5.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study of cocaine-dependent (stimulant) users vs matched controls using whole-brain optimized voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (corrected p-values) with coordinates and figures, provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study of gray matter in binge-drinking (alcohol) subjects and healthy controls. The methods specify whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (SPM8/DARTEL) and a Siemens 3T scanner; the paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons (t-tests) and voxelwise correlation results with coordinates for significant clusters. Although direct BD vs HV group differences were non-significant, the manuscript nevertheless reports whole-brain between-group contrasts, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to age-matched non-smokers with whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts reported (cluster-level FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates). The manuscript includes introduction, methods (participants, MRI field strength 3T, SPM8/DARTEL preprocessing), results (tables/figures with cluster coordinates), and discussion — i.e., full article text is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM MRI study comparing grey matter volume between nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoker controls (n=53 each). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (DARTEL-based VBM) with corrected results (AlphaSim-corrected P<0.05) and provides region-level results and cluster data (Tables/figures referenced). Participant demographics (age range, sex: all male), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 with DARTEL) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain evidence), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures), and I5 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software reported). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing young adult recreational cannabis users and matched controls using structural MRI. It reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses (with cluster thresholds, peak coordinates, Tables 2/3, and Figures) that directly compare gray matter between users and controls, as well as region volumes and shape analyses. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FreeSurfer, FIRST, SPSS) are reported. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for voxelwise/whole-brain GM comparisons. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volumes between young binge-drinking (alcohol) users and matched controls. The paper reports region-of-interest analyses but also presents an exploratory whole-brain between-group analysis (P<0.001 uncorrected, minimum cluster size reported) with MNI coordinates and cluster results, satisfying the requirement for at least one whole-brain contrast. Participant demographic details (age, sex distribution), MRI field strength (Siemens 1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI VBM study that reports whole-brain between-group contrasts of alcohol use disorder (AUD) subjects versus healthy controls (and gamblers) for grey matter volume. It uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry with voxelwise FDR correction and reports regional GM differences (text/figures), includes participant age and sex (male-only), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed VBM MRI study in English comparing gray matter volume between stimulant-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses (FWE-corrected, cluster and TFCE results) and specific cluster coordinates (e.g., nucleus accumbens) and presents whole-brain figures and ROI cross-validation. Methods and demographics are reported (participant age/sex, 3T field strength, VBM8/SPM8 preprocessing). Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion (E5) applies: the VBM/morphology results are reported for ROIs derived from the rsFC seed and target cluster (L.NAc and L.vmPFC) and appear to be ROI-based extractions rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group VBM contrast. The study is an empirical MRI study comparing prescription opioid users to controls and reports participant details and methods (meets I2 and I5). However it does not present a whole-brain GM volume between-group contrast required by I3, so it fails the whole-brain evidence inclusion criterion. Therefore exclude. (Excluded criterion met: E5. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criterion not met: I3.)

This study reports ROI-based analyses of seven subcortical structures and uses regression associations between continuous substance-use measures and volumes in population-based samples rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users vs. controls. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain between-group GM contrasts. Exclusion ID met: E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (does not present explicit GM volume comparisons between substance users and controls as between-group contrasts), I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise results), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing smokers and controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics (meets I5). However, the analyses focus on insular subregions (anterior/posterior insula) using FreeSurfer parcellation and ROI-based GMV comparisons and seed-based structural covariance; the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoker controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (smokers vs controls and smoker subgroups) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and provides ROI follow-up correlations. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, TBSS, AFNI, FSL) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. These elements satisfy the review's inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM differences in a substance-using group (nicotine). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of nicotine users vs controls that reports voxelwise gray-matter (VBM) analyses with whole-brain between-group comparisons. The Methods describe whole-brain VBM (FSL-VBM) and the Results report significant reductions in gray matter density in smokers (dlPFC and insula/operculum) with accompanying statistics. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study therefore meets the review’s requirements for empirical whole-brain GM contrast reporting for the nicotine drug class. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder (stimulant users) and healthy controls. The full text reports whole-brain analyses (SPM8/VBM8, DARTEL) and significant between-group cluster results (e.g., reduced MCC GM in CUD; cluster coordinates and statistics provided). Participant demographics and MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing 95 recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients vs 87 healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (2-sample t-test HC > ADP) with FWE whole-brain correction and provides peak coordinates for relevant regions (frontal cortex, cingulate, insula; medial OFC coordinates given). Voxelwise regression and Cox analyses use the same imaging data. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8, VBM8/DARTEL) and statistical methods are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a human MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (a stimulant class) with controls and reports voxel-based morphometry results focused on orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the analyses and reported voxelwise results are restricted to an a priori OFC region (ROI/small-volume focus) and the paper does not present a whole-brain between-group GM contrast of substance users vs controls. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I2 — empirical English-language MRI study comparing substance users (cocaine) and controls; I4 — voxelwise results are reported in figures/tables/supplementary material; I5 — participant age/sex and other sample descriptors are reported. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast is presented. Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis because it reports ROI-focused results without whole-brain between-group contrasts required by the review.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing chronic alcoholic men to controls and therefore meets I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences). However, the study reports lobar/regional volumetry (global cortical and six cortical regions) rather than a voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrast and does not provide coordinate-based whole-brain results in the text/abstract provided. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, the provided content appears to be limited to abstract/metadata and core article sections (methods/results/discussion) are not available here, so fulltext_incomplete=true. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast reported) and I4 (no voxelwise coordinates/tables of coordinates provided).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study using 3.0T MRI that directly compares gray matter density between 30 lifetime heroin-dependent individuals and 34 matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (optimized VBM, SPM2) identifying significant decreases in gray matter across prefrontal, anterior cingulate, insular and temporal cortices and presents partial correlation analyses with duration of heroin use. Participant age, sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing and statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, and core voxelwise results are clearly described. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, longitudinal MRI investigation of alcohol-related hippocampal volume change in college students; however it does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users vs controls. Instead, analyses used a hippocampus/parahippocampus mask and continuous regression of an alcohol use index (ROI-focused, not whole-brain case-control). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise results reported/available in main text/figures) and I5 (participant age, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not present a between-group substance-users vs controls comparison of GM volume) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given the mismatch with key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis, the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical human MRI study (PLoS One, 2018) comparing grey matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (one-way ANOVA) with results thresholded at FWE-corrected voxel level and provides peak coordinates and cluster sizes (text and figures), satisfying availability of whole-brain voxelwise results. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing and SPM8/DARTEL details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met; this is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an empirical MRI investigation comparing psychostimulant-dependent (cocaine, amphetamine) subjects to controls and reports gray matter volume differences for frontal and temporal lobes, but it uses manually traced region-of-interest (ROI) measures from a seven-slice coronal slab rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses or whole-brain between-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison) and I5 (participant demographics and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume is reported) and I4 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/whole-brain results provided). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to provide whole-brain/voxelwise GM comparisons required by the review (E5; unmet I3/I4).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI VBM study comparing heavy smokers (n=33) and never-smokers (n=22) that reports whole-brain between-group contrasts of grey matter volume (smokers < controls) with stereotactic coordinates (right Crus I, −32 −71 −32) and cluster-level correction. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical tools (SUIT toolbox, SPM5), and demographic information referenced in Table 1. The paper is a full-text article with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not an ROI-only paper, not a review). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent subjects that reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.0.0) — satisfying I5. However, the paper does not include a control group and does not report any whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users vs. controls (it analyzes regional/segmented gray-matter volumes within alcoholics and relates them to cognitive scores). Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (studies assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast) are not met. The study reports only regional/ROI-style segmented-volume analyses with no qualifying whole-brain between-group results, so exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) subjects and non-drug-using controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBM and VBM). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The authors performed whole-brain between-group contrasts with voxel-wise inference (FWE-corrected) and report the voxelwise results (no significant GM differences). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8; registration algorithms) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical human MRI data). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users (a stimulant class) and matched healthy controls. The full text includes methods (VBM8, MRI field strength 4T, preprocessing/statistical software), results, and reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (reduced medial orbitofrontal/ventromedial PFC gray matter in CUD) with tables/figures of coordinates. Therefore it provides qualifying whole-brain GM volume differences and meets the meta-analysis objective of identifying structural GM alterations in substance users. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study that directly compares grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid users and matched controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with SnPM non-parametric cluster inference (p<0.05 FWE). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts and regional results (including coordinates/cluster descriptions and ROI analyses), and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/SPM12, SnPM). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and limitations. Although participants are synthetic cannabinoid (SC) users rather than natural cannabis users, the study assesses GM alterations related to cannabinoid receptor agonist use and thus fits the review objective as stated. Therefore all inclusion criteria I2–I5 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical voxel-based morphometry study in English comparing grey matter volume between occasional amphetamine-type stimulant/cocaine users (N=165) and matched controls (N=46). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (linear mixed effects) and whole-brain regressions with cluster-corrected results and coordinates (VBM results presented in text/tables/supplement). Methods include participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FAST4, FNIRT, AFNI, R/SPSS). This satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; is an original empirical human MRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (substance users) with healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts (patients vs controls), cluster results with MNI coordinates, imaging acquisition (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8), participant demographics (age/sex), and cue type. All core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons in substance (alcohol) users.

This study is an empirical, longitudinal MRI study of alcohol effects on rhesus macaques and reports regional gray-matter volume changes with ethanol intake. However, it does not address the review objective of human substance users versus non-using controls: (a) the sample is non-human (rhesus macaques) and (b) there is no between-group contrast of substance users versus non-using controls (comparisons are heavy vs non-heavy drinkers and within-subject baseline vs drinking). Therefore it fails key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria: none of the listed exclusion IDs (E5, E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics details are provided). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study does not provide GM comparisons between substance users and non-using controls in humans), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs non-user controls), I4 (while whole-brain parcellation results are reported, the study does not present the required between-group user vs control voxelwise contrasts/coordinate tables relevant to this meta-analysis). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Empirical VBM study of cocaine-dependent humans (stimulant class) with whole-brain voxelwise GM volume comparisons vs matched controls. Methods report VBM preprocessing (SPM8/DARTEL), 3T MRI, participant demographics (age, all male, African-American), and results include voxelwise group contrasts (figures and cluster-based in-text results) and imaging–behavior correlations. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Primary exclusion: the study examines adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (in utero exposure), not current substance users versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (whole-brain/vertex-wise surface-based gray matter asymmetry maps are reported) and I4 (voxelwise/vertexwise mapping reported as quantitative maps). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study does not compare substance users to controls as defined by the review — participants are exposed prenatally rather than being substance-using subjects). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E5, E6) are directly met. Because the population does not match the review’s target and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded.

The study is an empirical English-language VBM MRI study reporting whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses relating substance use (number of substances and dose-response) to gray matter volume and provides methodological details (age/sex, field strength, preprocessing). However, it does not report a clear whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users versus controls (i.e., a direct group comparison of users vs controls). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3, which requires at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study), I4 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in text/figures), I5 (sufficient methodological details). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it reports cortical thickness (CT) analyses rather than grey matter (GM) volume differences. The meta-analysis requires empirical MRI studies comparing GM volume between substance users and controls (I2) and at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume (I3). While this paper is an empirical English MRI study and provides whole-brain voxelwise results/tables and details on participants, MRI field strength, and preprocessing (satisfying I4 and I5), it does not report GM volume contrasts or voxelwise GM volume results—only CT. Therefore I2 and I3 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports lobar/subcortical ROI volumetric analyses rather than any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or coordinate-based results. Exclusion criterion: E5 (ROI-only, no qualifying whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users [alcohol-dependent] and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and methodological details). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast or coordinate tables reported). Full text appears complete for screening (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing heavy cannabis users (n=11) to non-using controls (n=8) with whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. The paper reports voxel-wise results with cluster statistics and MNI coordinates (including hippocampal small-volume correction), details participant demographics (all male, matched on age/education/SES), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99). These satisfy inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM study), I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results reported with coordinates/clusters), and I5 (key methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study should be included for the meta-analysis of GM alterations in substance (cannabis) users.

This is an empirical MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing substance-dependent individuals (n=19) to controls (n=20). The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM analyses (ANCOVA) with cluster-level FWE correction and voxel coordinates for medial OFC differences (i.e., qualifying whole-brain results). Methods report participant age/sex, 3-T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1/SPM5). Although subjects were polysubstance-dependent, the study examines GM differences between substance users and controls and thus addresses the review objective covering relevant drug classes (stimulants, alcohol, etc.). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, empirical human MRI data). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical MRI study of cigarette (nicotine) users vs controls with reported participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, SPSS), and analysis of grey-matter volumes. However, the study reports region-based volumetric (subcortical ROI) measures and whole-brain summary volumes (TBV, TVV, ICV) rather than a spatially resolved whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or coordinate-based results. The review's inclusion requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume; studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results are excluded (E5). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This longitudinal MRI study examines brain structural changes associated with adolescent alcohol initiation and reports whole-brain surface-based cortical thickness and white-matter/DTI contrasts with cluster coordinates. However, the review’s inclusion criterion I2 requires empirical MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences. This paper reports cortical thickness (surface-based measure) rather than GM volume (e.g., VBM-derived GM volume) and therefore does not meet I2. It also does not perform whole-brain between-group contrasts specifically of GM volume (I3 not met). The full text is complete and provides coordinates and preprocessing details. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise/vertexwise results reported in tables/figures) and I5 (reporting of age/sex, scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered, but the absence of GM volume analyses means the study must be excluded per the protocol. Full text complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing gray matter volume between heroin (opioid) abusers and healthy controls. The full text includes methods, results and discussion and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (widespread GMV atrophy and specific cluster-level findings with AlphaSim correction) and provides voxelwise results in figures/tables. Participant age and sex distributions are reported; MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FLIRT, FNIRT, FAST, SPSS) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical human data). Full text appears complete.

This VBM study includes cocaine use disorder (CUD) and control groups and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses, but the manuscript explicitly reports PENK main effects and Diagnosis × PENK interactions and states that group differences between CUD and controls have been previously explored in this sample and are not reported here. Therefore the paper does not provide a whole-brain between-group (substance users vs controls) GM contrast or coordinates that the meta-analysis requires. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI VBM study with substance users and controls), I4 (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported/available as interactions), I5 (reports MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software and participant info). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no reported whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls comparing GM volume in this paper). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently, the study cannot contribute the required between-group GM coordinates and should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed MRI study comparing subjects with alcohol use disorder and matched healthy controls using whole-brain surface-based and volumetric analyses of gray matter (FreeSurfer/Qdec). The manuscript reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (cortical thickness and gray matter volume) with multiple-comparison correction (Monte Carlo), and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Results are presented in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between heroin-dependent individuals and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (FDR-corrected, cluster threshold k>200) showing reduced GM volume in prefrontal and other regions. Key methodological details are provided: participant demographics (N, age/sex summary), MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1), and correlation analyses. Results are presented in the main text with regional findings and statistical thresholds; supplementary data are referenced for further details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing gray-matter regional volumes in alcohol-dependent participants versus controls and reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software details (meets I2 and I5). However, the study uses atlas-based lobar and subregional volume comparisons and selected subcortical/cerebellar ROIs rather than reporting at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or providing coordinate-based whole-brain results. Therefore it does not meet I3. Because it reports only region-based/ROI analyses without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study of cocaine (stimulant) users versus controls, reporting gray-matter differences and voxelwise cluster coordinates (meets I2 and I4). MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) and participant demographics are described (meets I5). However, the analysis was restricted to a set of a priori small volume templates/ROIs with small-volume correction and did not present a whole-brain between-group GM contrast; therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and falls under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).
