This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volume between cannabis users and non-users using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (SPM8/VBM8). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (Non-Users > Users) and identifies specific clusters (lingual gyrus, anterior cingulum right/left, rolandic operculum) with family-wise error results for the right anterior cingulum. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, MarsBaR, SPSS) are reported. Lifetime exposure and relevant covariates (alcohol, cigarettes, prenatal exposures, SES, familial risk) are described and controlled. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical, English-language VBM study of gray matter in alcohol users and reports whole-brain voxelwise results and sufficient methodological details, it does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. The imaging analyses are multiple-regression/correlation analyses using AUDIT scores across a continuum of participants rather than an explicit substance-user vs control group voxelwise comparison. Therefore it does not meet the required inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I4 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported/available), I5 (participant demographics, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not address the review objective of comparing substance users to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (demographic and MRI/preprocessing details reported: participant age/sex, MRI field strengths, FSL preprocessing and SPSS noted). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls — sample is first-episode schizophrenia patients vs healthy controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls reported), I4 (not applicable — no voxelwise substance-user contrasts presented). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because it fails to satisfy the core inclusion criteria (I2 and I3).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volumes between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (CD vs controls and sex-specific contrasts) using SPM8/DARTEL with cluster-level FWE correction, and provides anatomical cluster descriptions and coordinates/figures (tables and figures). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical MRI study comparing alcoholic patients to controls and reports cortical gray matter and CSF volume changes using a segmentation approach. However, analyses are based on predefined global measures and 6 region-of-interest (ROI) cortical regions rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (no voxelwise coordinate tables or mass-univariate whole-brain results are reported). Therefore it violates E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics and MRI field strength/methods). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast) and I4 (no voxelwise coordinate results reported). Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review/overview of structural MRI findings in fetal alcohol spectrum disorders rather than an original empirical MRI study reporting new whole‑brain voxelwise GM volume contrasts between substance users and controls. It does not present new participant-level whole-brain GM results or coordinate tables required for meta-analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study) and I3 (reports at least one whole‑brain between‑group GM contrast). It meets exclusion criterion E6 (non‑empirical review without original human MRI data).

Exclusion E5 applies: the study reports only region-of-interest (OFC and hippocampus) gray-matter volume analyses and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences related to alcohol use) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength=3T, and preprocessing software=Freesurfer). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (meets I2). However, the paper uses an atlas-based ROI approach (lobar and Brodmann-area aggregation) and reports region-of-interest volume comparisons rather than any whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain between-group contrast. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results) and does not meet I3. The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: exclude because no whole-brain/voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast was reported.

This is an empirical human MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (whole-brain VBM) comparing alcohol-dependent participants (N=130) to healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (permutation testing, corrected) with figures/tables describing clusters, and provides participant demographics (age/sex), scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, BET, FAST, FLIRT, FNIRT). The study addresses the meta-analysis objective for the alcohol pharmacological class. It is not ROI-only and is original empirical work, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts with MNI coordinates and tables/figures of results, specifies participant demographics (all right-handed males, age ranges/means reported), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I2, I3, I4, I5). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent (substance-using) patients and matched healthy controls. The full text reports a whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group analysis with results surviving p<0.05 FWE correction and provides MNI coordinates for a significant left IFG cluster. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only study; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language VBM study comparing methamphetamine (a stimulant) users to healthy controls and reporting whole-brain voxelwise GM volume contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; MRI acquisition (1.5T), preprocessing (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL), statistical analyses, participant age/sex (66 males, 18–50), and coordinates for significant whole-brain clusters (FWE- and FDR-corrected results) are provided. The study therefore addresses the review objective (stimulant-class GM differences) and meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing grey matter volume between 33 heavy cannabis users and 42 matched controls using voxel-wise whole-brain analysis (SPM8/VBM8) on 3T data. The paper reports between-group GM contrasts (voxel-wise VBM with both ROI small-volume correction and whole-brain thresholds), and describes whole-brain statistical thresholds and null results outside ROIs. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. It is not excluded by E5 (not ROI-only: performed voxelwise whole-brain VBM analyses, with ROI small-volume correction but whole-brain thresholds specified) or E6. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study that directly compares grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients (substance users) and matched healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain VBM between-group results (GM reductions in ADP vs HC reported both inside and outside predefined ROIs, with whole-brain tables/Supporting Information), and describes imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM), and participant demographics (age/sex matching). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; it is empirical human MRI data). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language multimodal MRI study comparing 22 AUD patients to 18 healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (GM density) and DTI. The paper reports whole-brain spatial maps (joint-ICA components) showing GM clusters that significantly differentiate AUD from controls and provides anatomical localization (figures and atlas-based labeling). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/CAT12, FSL, TBSS, Fusion ICA Toolbox), and participant demographics (age range, sex balance) are reported. Voxelwise whole-brain results are presented as component spatial maps (and described in detail), which satisfy the review’s allowance for voxelwise results reported in figures/tables. No ROI-only restriction applies. Therefore the study meets I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and controls (I2 met). The paper reports detailed participant demographics and MRI acquisition/processing details (I5 met). However, the volumetric analyses are focused on the hippocampus (voxel-based morphometric estimation and ROI/anterodorsal hippocampus analyses) rather than reporting at least one whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast of substance users vs controls. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3 not met) and falls under the exclusion criterion for ROI-only studies with no qualifying whole-brain results (E5). Full text appears complete.

Excluded (E5): This is an empirical English MRI study that includes manual volumetric (ROI) measurements of selected gray-matter structures (I2 satisfied). However, it does not report any whole‑brain voxelwise gray-matter volume contrast or VBM-style whole-brain GM analyses comparing substance users vs controls (I3 not met). The voxelwise results reported pertain to DTI metrics (FA/ADC), not direct GM volume maps; thus qualifying whole‑brain GM evidence is absent. Inclusion IDs met: I2. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no whole‑brain GM between-group contrast), I4 not applicable (voxelwise results available are DTI metrics rather than GM volume). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder (substance users) to healthy controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts and regressions (2×2 ANCOVA and multiple regression) with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results. Participant demographics (age, sex) and scanner details (3T Siemens) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM pipeline) are reported. Voxelwise results are reported in the text with coordinates and figures/tables referenced. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter between 61 methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) subjects and 44 controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (MA vs controls) with cluster-level correction and provides methods details (participant age range/sex, 3T Siemens scanner, FSL-VBM preprocessing and statistical software). Results of whole-brain analyses (clusters of increased/decreased GM density) are reported in the main text and figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical MRI VBM study with whole-brain voxelwise results relating gray matter volume to smoking cessation outcome (quitters vs relapsers). However, it does NOT include a between-group comparison of substance users versus non-using controls. Inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls) are not met. The paper does report voxelwise whole-brain VBM results (I4 satisfied) and provides imaging/preprocessing details, but that does not fulfill the requirement for user-vs-control comparisons. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing chronic cigarette smokers (nicotine users) with matched non-smoking controls. The paper reports voxel-wise two-sample t-test whole-brain contrasts (VBM) with cluster/figure/table results described in the results and figure/table references. Participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), MRI field strength (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users (nicotine) versus controls.

This is an empirical MRI study of smokers vs controls (I2 satisfied) that reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), and FreeSurfer preprocessing (I5 satisfied). However, the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses (FreeSurfer-derived regional/ bilateral ROI volumes and corpus callosum subregions) and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts, coordinate tables, or voxelwise results in text/figures/supplementary material. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on E5.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study assessing gray matter/white matter regional volumes in alcohol-dependent individuals versus light-drinking controls (meets I2). However, the analyses reported are automated segmentation into lobes and subcortical structures (regional/lobar volume comparisons) rather than voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrasts with spatial coordinates. The manuscript does not present whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts that would qualify under the review’s whole-brain evidence requirement (I3). Therefore it effectively reports region-of-interest/regional analyses only and meets exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing gray matter density between current smokers and matched never-smoker controls using voxel-based morphometry (SPM2). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (multiple regression on SPM2) identifying regions of decreased GM density in smokers (posterior cingulum/precuneus, frontal gyri, right thalamus), and notes statistical thresholds and cluster extents. Participant age/sex, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/MATLAB) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of structural GM differences in nicotine users.

This is an empirical MRI study comparing chronic alcohol users to controls (meets I2). However, the available/full text appears to be limited to abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study reports region-based hippocampal and temporal lobe volumetry (ROI-style measures) and does not present a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast in the provided content; therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study); I5 partially (age/sex reported in abstract). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only). Because the full text here appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata shown), I flagged fulltext_incomplete=true; confirmation requires access to complete methods/results to verify presence/absence of whole-brain analyses.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing alcoholic participants and controls and reports detailed cerebellar grey- and white-matter volumes (manual parcellation), participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and statistical methods. However, it does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast of grey matter volume; analyses are restricted to cerebellar parcellation/ROI measures rather than whole-brain GM comparisons. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on abstract, this is an empirical MRI study comparing gray matter in alcoholic patients vs controls (I2 satisfied). However, the available content does not confirm whether results come from whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (I3 cannot be verified). Cannot rule out ROI-only analyses (E5) without methods/results. Therefore exclude pending access to full text. Inclusion met: I2. Inclusion not met/uncertain: I3. Exclusion met: none.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent users and controls using voxel-based morphometry. The study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANCOVA in SPM5) with FWE-corrected results and cluster coordinates, and presents tables/figures of voxelwise findings. Participant demographics (age range, gender), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, unified segmentation VBM) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent participants versus healthy controls that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and prospectively related gray matter volumes to relapse risk. The full text contains introduction, methods (MRI acquisition, SPM8/DARTEL preprocessing), results (whole-brain cluster-wise contrasts with coordinates and figures), and discussion. Participant age and sex are reported; preprocessing/statistical software is specified; MRI acquisition details (sequence and voxel size) are provided. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for empirical MRI studies comparing substance users to controls with whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate reporting and is appropriate for inclusion.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol users (recovering vs actively drinking) with whole-brain volumetric analyses, but it does NOT compare substance users to non-using controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs NOT met: I2 (does not assess GM differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded from the review focused on user vs control GM volume contrasts.

Full text appears incomplete: provided HTML contains only page shell without introduction, methods, results, or discussion, so core study details are missing. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (cannot confirm this is an empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls from the available content), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts are reported in the provided content), I4 (no voxelwise coordinates/figures/tables are available), I5 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are not reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (cannot determine ROI-only or non-empirical status from incomplete text). Because the full text is incomplete (fulltext_incomplete=true) the study cannot be assessed for inclusion and is excluded from the review at this stage.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that compares young adult moderate-to-heavy alcohol users (n=35) with light-drinking controls (n=27). The paper reports whole-brain gray matter volume comparisons (decreased total gray matter volume in users vs controls) and provides methods for MRI acquisition (3.0 T), preprocessing (VBM8 in SPM8), and participant demographics (age/sex). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM volume comparisons between substance (alcohol) users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between amphetamine-type stimulant (ATS) users and controls (experienced users, low-exposure users, and drug‑naive controls). The paper reports whole‑brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM results with corrected clusters) showing GM reductions in medial frontal regions in experienced users versus controls. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL, TBSS, FSL‑VBM) and analysis details are provided. This is not an ROI-only or non-empirical paper. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM MRI study comparing early-onset chronic cannabis users (n=29) to matched controls (n=28) reporting voxel-wise whole-brain between-group contrasts of gray matter volume. The manuscript includes full methods (participants, MRI field strength 1.5T, SPM8/VBM preprocessing, genotyping), results (whole-brain between-group contrast showing increased GM in left postcentral gyrus at P<0.001 uncorrected; interaction analyses repeated at whole-brain level), and figures/tables with coordinate results. Thus it meets the meta-analysis aim of identifying GM differences in cannabis users vs controls and provides whole-brain voxelwise results in the main text and figures. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study in humans that includes voxelwise whole-brain VBM analysis comparing gray matter density between cigarette users (smokers/ex-smokers) and controls. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and whole-brain non-parametric testing), Results (stating VBM revealed no statistical differences), and Discussion. Although the VBM results are null, the study performed a whole-brain between-group GM contrast (satisfying the requirement to report voxelwise whole-brain analyses), and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/processing details. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for structural GM comparisons and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed MRI study comparing gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) users (n=84) and healthy controls (n=86) using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (voxelwise findings with coordinates and figures/tables referenced), and discussion. It reports participant age range and sex counts, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8). Whole-brain between-group contrasts are reported (FWE-corrected voxel and cluster thresholds) with coordinates (e.g., ventral putamen x=24,y=15,z=-11) and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical human data). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of structurally altered GM in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter between alcohol-dependent patients (n=22) and age-/sex-matched controls (n=22). The full text contains introduction, methods (including MRI field strength 1.5T, preprocessing, SPM2, modulation, smoothing), results (whole-brain voxelwise GM and WM contrasts reported with tables/figures and statistics), and discussion. It reports participant age and sex, imaging parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study in English), I3 (reports whole-brain between-group GM contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures), and I5 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical human MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing smokers (current/past) versus nonsmokers, with regional gray matter differences identified (right fusiform and right temporal subgyral GM in female smokers). The full text includes methods (participants, MRI acquisition at 1.5T, preprocessing with SPM2), results (voxelwise analyses and identified regions), and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users — nicotine smokers — and controls), I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls using GM volume), I4 (voxelwise results are reported/described and referenced), and I5 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study of alcohol consumption reporting whole-brain voxelwise associations, but it does not present a between-group comparison of substance users versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (reports whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study does not compare a substance-user group to a control group; instead it models alcohol consumption continuously in a community sample) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls is reported). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails key inclusion criteria I2 and I3 required by the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical MRI study of 55 male drinkers relating biomarkers (GGT, MCV, CDT) to regional gray-matter volumes via regression, but it does not include a control group or any between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring (I2) assessment of GM volume differences between substance users and controls and (I3) at least one whole-brain between-group contrast. The paper also does not report voxelwise between-group coordinates or maps (I4). It does report participant sex, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/segmentation methods, satisfying I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are directly applicable. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because inclusion criteria I2 and I3 (and I4) are not met; I5 is met. Full text appears complete.

This is an MRI study but it does not report whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts of substance users versus controls. The study uses manual ROI tracing of the lingula and reports associations/correlations between lingula thickness and self-reported alcohol/drug use in a community sample (not a case-control comparison of substance users vs controls). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI comparing substance users and controls) and I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrasts). It also does not provide voxelwise whole-brain results as allowed by I4. It does report participant age/sex and MRI field strength, satisfying I5. It meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing gray matter volume between heroin-dependent patients on methadone maintenance (n=27) and matched healthy controls (n=23). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts using DARTEL-based VBM (SPM5/VBM5) with cluster-level FWE correction and presents regional GMV differences and correlations with clinical measures; coordinate results are referenced in tables/figures. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are reported. Thus it meets the review objective (opioid class) and inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM analyses. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports VBM structural analyses but the statistical VBM comparisons were restricted to the (para)hippocampal region using a small-volume correction (ROI-focused), with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study comparing GM between cannabis users and controls) and I5 (participant demographics, scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only ROI/small-volume VBM results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter (GM) volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The full text includes introduction, methods (VBM preprocessing, SPM8, VBM8, 3T field strength), results (whole-brain ANCOVA reporting GM reductions across predefined ROIs and whole-brain tables), and discussion. Whole-brain between-group contrasts (ADP vs HC) are reported and coordinates/regions are provided; voxelwise results and tables are available. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study that reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain between-group comparisons of gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) users and matched controls. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion; VBM results are reported (greater GM volume in right caudate nucleus and right orbitofrontal gyri) from a whole-brain analysis. Participant information (n, sex), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical tools (SPM8, FNIRT) are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only study or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of substance users (heavy drinkers) vs controls and reports lobar/neocortical GM volumetric differences, but it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results. The paper uses atlas-based lobar ROI volumetry (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital lobes) rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses or tables of coordinates; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study of GM volume differences) and I5 (reporting of participant age/sex and MRI field strength and processing methods). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is not available (only metadata/abstract-level access), so I cannot verify whether whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts are reported. The study also examines individuals with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (in utero exposure), not current substance users, which does not match the review population of substance users vs controls. Therefore it fails to meet the required whole-brain reporting criterion and the population/construct required for this review. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM differences). Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast — not verifiable), I4 (reporting of voxelwise results — not verifiable). Exclusion IDs met: none. fulltext incomplete prevents definitive assessment.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T MRI. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected results) identifying regions with reduced GM in alcohol users (cingulate, precentral, middle frontal, cerebellum, insula, etc.) and provides methodological details (participants’ age/sex, scanner field strength, VBM8/SPM8 processing). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons between substance (alcohol) users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing grey matter volume between substance user groups (former regular users, FRUs) and comparison groups (former light users, FLUs) across alcohol, cocaine (stimulant), and cannabis. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (exploratory whole-brain analyses with cluster correction) and voxelwise ROI analyses, and provides coordinate-level results (e.g., left globus pallidus coordinates) and detailed methods (MRI field strength, acquisition, preprocessing, statistical software, participant age and covariates). Although the control/comparison group consists of former light users rather than substance-naïve individuals, the study still provides qualifying between-group whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies the inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing active heavy alcohol users (HD) and matched light-drinking controls (LD) with quantitative assessment of gray matter (GM) volumes. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise deformation morphometry analyses (group contrasts HD vs LD and regression with drinking severity), describes permutation-based correction and cluster analyses, and presents statistical maps (figures) of voxelwise GM/CSF/WM differences. Participant age/sex and MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical methods (probabilistic segmentation, atlas-based ROI, deformation tensor morphometry, SAS, fMRIstat) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing grey matter volume between chronic cocaine (stimulant) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses (cluster-wise permutation testing, maps and coordinates provided) and secondary voxelwise regressions within the abnormal mask (coordinates and figures included). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (FSLVBM/FLIRT/FNIRT) and analysis software (CamBA) are reported. These satisfy the review’s requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise GM comparisons of a targeted drug class (stimulants). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs healthy controls and reports hippocampal subfield volumetry using FreeSurfer (meets I2 and I5). However, the study reports only region-specific segmentation/ROI analyses (hippocampal subfields CA2+3, CA4+DG, subiculum) and longitudinal changes within those subfields. There are no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts or coordinate-based results presented that would qualify for inclusion. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (whole-brain evidence) and I4 (voxelwise/coordinate results) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical MRI study in English comparing gray matter volumes in alcohol-dependent patients versus controls (I2 met). However, the structural analyses reported are restricted to predefined regions-of-interest (ROIs) derived from fMRI results rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported) and I4 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/figures of between-group GM differences provided). The full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because E5 applies; I2 met but I3 and I4 not met.

Exclusion E5 met: the study reports significant findings only from an ROI VBM analysis (amygdala) and states that whole-brain analyses (skulled and skull-stripped, i.e., entire-brain) produced no significant voxels — therefore there are no qualifying whole-brain results/coordinates to include. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study comparing GM volume between substance users [alcohol-dependent/abstinent] and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM results reported — whole-brain analyses yielded no significant voxels), I4 (no whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/results available for inclusion; only ROI results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text provided appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata available). The abstract describes regional brain volume analyses in alcoholics drawn from prior neuroimaging studies, but does not report or confirm any whole‑brain voxelwise GM between-group contrasts. Therefore I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) cannot be verified and is not met. I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) appears satisfied. No exclusion criteria can be definitively applied from the available text (ROI-only status is likely but not confirmed). Because the required whole-brain voxelwise result (I3) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, this study is excluded pending access to the complete article reporting whole-brain GM contrasts.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing chronic alcoholic men with healthy controls and reporting differences in cortical gray matter volume (smaller cortical gray matter) and related whole-brain CSF/ventricle measures. The paper includes methods, results, and discussion describing whole-brain cortical gray- and white-matter volumetry derived from segmented MRI and reports between-group contrasts at admission and discharge. Thus it meets I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I3 (reports whole-brain between-group GM volume comparisons). While not all preferred reporting details (e.g., scanner field strength or specific preprocessing/statistical software) are explicit, I5 is advisory and missing details do not preclude inclusion. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion for analyses of GM volume differences in alcohol users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes in crack-cocaine dependent men versus controls (I2 satisfied). The manuscript reports regional cortical volumes using predefined Talairach-based ROIs (prefrontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or coordinate-based results. It does not provide voxelwise/coordinate tables or figures that would qualify as whole-brain mass-univariate results, so it fails the whole-brain requirement (I3 not met; I4 not met). Because the analysis is ROI-based with no qualifying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4. Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (FASD) versus controls that reports ROI-based ACC measures (volume, surface area, thickness) and brain–behavior correlations. However, it does not examine current substance users versus controls and does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM-volume contrasts. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I2 (study population = substance users vs controls) and I3 (whole-brain GM between-group results). It does meet I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics software). It also meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
